answers.answer: Taking the title during Act makes it Usurper-side only at the next Exile turn's Wake: that Wake checks victory before flipping an Exile Oathkeeper to Usurper. The Exile can first win at the following Wake, or at the end of round 8 if that comes first while they still hold the title Usurper-side. If the title is lost before then, the Usurper win is prevented; retaking it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘two timing windows’; checked before flip; next Wake or end of round 8; losing title prevents win and retaking resets.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary also requires a revealed true Vision, the goal completed at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player; a tie does not qualify.
answers.evidence: Oath table and Visionary victory paragraph: global 3-Visions requirement and ‘strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ends of rounds 5, 6, 7; outcomes 6 / 5–6 / 3–6; Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents roll.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor. A Citizen's Successor goal alone does not end the game.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion: round 8 exact priority 1–4; Successor replacement and Vision priority listed.

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by revealed Vision or by becoming Usurper; Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oath table lists Successor goals; Visionary paragraph says Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either place 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 of its favor to a least-full suit bank, choosing among tied banks. Never take its last favor: with 1 on it, add one if able; if you have none, do nothing. If already Mob-side, make this choice a second time. After the payment choice(s), check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip to Mob if so. If it becomes Mob at this final check, do not retroactively make the second choice this Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1: choice, last-favor rule, repeat if already Mob, then 6+ check; a newly flipped banner does not repeat.

answers.answer: Rest in order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Exile/Chancellor Supply according to warbands remaining in personal bank (Chancellor: 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile: 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4); Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; move the Supply marker one space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); then optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order steps 1–5, including Citizen exact marker and saved unspent Supply.

answers.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that base world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 (or fewer if source runs out, a world Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it); no voluntary early stop. From the world deck, reveal one at a time and stop immediately on a Vision, advancing the Visions Drawn track. A Vision from the discard pile does not stop drawing or advance that track.
answers.evidence: Search section gives source choice, costs, draw amount and distinct world-deck versus discard Vision rules.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; do not use the same-region pile. For hand/adviser discards, choose the destination based on your pawn's region: Cradle to Provinces, Provinces to Hinterland, Hinterland to Cradle. If discarding a card at a site in another region, use that card's region for the cycle instead of your pawn's. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; its secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations paragraph specifies cycle, remote-site exception, and where favor/secrets go.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, apply the new limit before playing it (and use the lowest of multiple limits). Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card can be held facedown. Later, as a minor action, play a facedown adviser faceup to a legal destination or discard it. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. An Exile who plays a true Vision reveals it in the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding the previous revealed Vision; it is not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens can hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser and true Vision options; Minor actions: play/discard facedown adviser and replace prior revealed Vision.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply. At your pawn's site, choose an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets); place 1 favor on it and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (Citizens gain purple). Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site and cannot Muster remotely. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site. For 1 secret placed on it, gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Alternatively place 2 favor on it to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser; with no matching adviser this yields zero secrets. Facedown advisers do not match. Take only available favor/warbands if the source is short; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections specify costs, eligible cards, gains, matching, and limitations.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets) and take it faceup into your personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank; pay any amount of its resource strictly greater than its current amount. For People's Favor, put the payment on it, distribute its old favor singly to suit banks in order from a chosen bank, and flip it to normal if Mob; there is no seizure penalty. For Darkest Secret, put payment on it; take 1 old secret and give the previous holder the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from the shared bank, the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: Recover section details target, cost, payment and distinct old-resource handling for each banner.

answers.answer: Another player's Darkest Secret is recoverable only if a suited card at that holder's pawn site matches none of that player's faceup advisers. If there is no suited site card, it is protected; an empty site and a ruin-only site protect it. With no faceup advisers, a suited card at the site matches none and the Secret is recoverable. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. This protection does not apply when recovering it from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: Corrected Darkest Secret protection paragraph expressly covers no faceup advisers, empty sites, and ruin-only sites.

answers.answer: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map (one defense die each). If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may target their relics there (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to their resources), or pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located relic target satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 specify defender eligibility, mandatory local target, remote sites, and co-located targets.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force, then applies relevant modifiers. Defense dice include those for targets and modifiers, plus the mandatory title bonus (Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2). On defense, count rolled shields, doubling shields for each double-symbol (multipliers stack), then add defending warbands at targeted sites and defender board force if the defender's pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site; doubles do not multiply warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. On attack, each skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands; count full swords and one attack for each pair of hollow swords (a leftover single is zero). The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 each, but if sacrificing, must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender win.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4–5 give dice, defense additions, skulls, swords, exact sacrifice rule and strict-win condition.

answers.answer: After an attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites, and takes all targeted relics/banners. Zero garrisons leaves the site to bandits unless another power applies. For a banner seized by any method except Recover, burn 2 resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood can override the attacker's destination choice. Resolve attacker-target results, then victorious plan effects, then any ‘At end, discard’ effects.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 give defeat-before-target order, zero placement, banner seizure, banishment and final effect order.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens can join with defender permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. The defender and Allies share relevant Campaign modifiers and the meanings of ‘you,’ ‘your enemy,’ and ‘defender’ as one side; ‘your site/board’ still means each player's own. Allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. They can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; the user pays and a plan is used only once. The declared defender decides disputed order/timing/priority. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizens' board warbands stay there. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; Chancellor attacking a Citizen makes that Citizen non-Imperial. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.
answers.evidence: Campaign defender qualification and Imperial defense bullets specify allies, shared powers, plans, casualties, and temporary status.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs before modifiers, by origin and destination: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Move to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. Reveal a facedown destination, place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank, and place its printed number of relics facedown from the relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: an applicable ‘spend no Supply’ power makes Supply cost zero despite increases, including for banishment; site-entry restrictions still apply unless specifically ignored.
answers.evidence: Travel section includes full origin/destination cost table, reveal procedure, modifier order and free-Travel override.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder, even an Exile, may offer Citizenship to any Exile including themself, but cannot use Scepter powers on the turn they took it. In later turns an offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; it may also negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics. Acceptance flips the recipient to Citizen, replaces their board/map warbands with purple (recipient chooses removals if purple supply is short), discards a revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes Supply to full leftmost. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship uses conversion steps without a required offer, relic gift, or invented exchange; a modifier is uncovered only if a Reliquary relic is actually removed.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, and Forced Citizenship paragraphs.

answers.answer: For the next Oath, a win by Vision alone means choose the Oath matching that Vision; any other victory method or multiple methods lets the winner choose any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, flip every Citizen board, including boxed ones, to Exile. The winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; no in-play Scepter permission, payment, or Reliquary gift is required. Each acceptor must flip to Citizen and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. Rebuild the deck by shuffling all denizens remaining in play (excluding cards at sites, in Archive, or Dispossessed), then make a top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 total), a middle stack of 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 total), and put remaining denizens beneath. The Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; the intended top stack is 10+2=12, not 14.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9 specify Oath choice, Citizen turnover/acceptance, and 10 denizens + 2 Visions (12), correcting the aid.
